verses.text: 601. The Scriptures had foretold this divine plan of salvation through the putting to death of “the righteous one, my Servant” as a mystery of universal redemption, that is, as the ransom that would free men from the slavery of sin. (Is 53:11; cf. 53:12; Jn 8:34-36; Acts 3:14.) Citing a confession of faith that he himself had “received,” St. Paul professes that “Christ died for our sins in accordance with the scriptures.” (1 Cor 15:3; cf. Acts 3:18; 7:52; 13:29; 26:22-23.) In particular Jesus‘ redemptive death fulfils Isaiah’s prophecy of the suffering Servant. (Cf. Is 53:7-8 and Acts 8:32-35.) Indeed Jesus himself explained the meaning of his life and death in the light of God’s suffering Servant. (Cf. Mt 20:28.) After his Resurrection he gave this interpretation of the Scriptures to the disciples at Emmaus, and then to the apostles. (Cf. Lk 24:25-27, 44-45.)
